checklist.notes: The concrete routines and form dialogue suit A1.2, but the unsupported instructions contain ‘private information’, ‘versions’, ‘syllable boundaries’, ‘explicitly’, and dense multi-condition self-checks beyond the tier.
Present-simple routines, the movement sense of run, the two-syllable guidance for after/address, and the request-response grammar are accurate.
The model dialogue is plausible. A vague collocation in the final production instruction is recorded as a minor issue.
Internal comparison showed only expected reuse of the present-simple frame and authorized target language; external originality remains untested.
The lesson reviews only the authorized present simple, help function, syllables, movement run, and personal-information topic with phonemes as context.
All content is English and embedded references remain within the exact regenerated request scope.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: Essential A1.2 directions are phrased in abstract teacher language (‘rehearse syllable boundaries’, ‘both versions must keep’, ‘the helper explicitly carries’, and a four-part final check). The linguistic load is likely to obscure what beginners must say and write.
findings.recommendation: Convert each task to short numbered steps with a worked model and use simple wording or Vietnamese support for privacy and pronunciation concepts.

findings.description: ‘Ask another person to write one fact’ is grammatical but vague and not the usual collocation for the address/detail task.
findings.recommendation: Use ‘ask another person to write down one detail.’

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
